newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power again steady in warm weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power again steady in warm weather.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady again Wednesday at relatively low levels due to mild weather, industry sources said.
"We've got mild temperatures, healthy (generation) units, and not a whole lot going on," said one Mid-West power trader.
Traders again said they expected prices to move higher next week when below-normal temperatures were forecast through much of the Mid-West.
Temperatures in the Mid-West just south of the Great Lakes were above normal Wednesday with maximums in the high-30s and mid-40s degrees Fahrenheit.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Thursday delivery were pegged steady at $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were also assessed steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In MAIN, peak, non-firm power for Thursday delivery was said to be lower at $19.00-20.00 from $20.00-21.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
January/February MAIN peak power was said to be talked steady at $25.50-26.00 per MWh.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday were discussed unchanged at $18.00-19.00, the sources said.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power was assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
January/February peak ECAR prices were pegged steady to lower at $23.50-24.00 from $23.75-24.25 per MWh on Tuesday.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were talked steady at $16.00-17.00, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were said to have moved lower into the $9.00-11.00 range from $11.00-13.00 on Tuesday.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged up slightly at $25.25-25.50, the sources said.
